questions.question: A teacher posts the quiz scores for seven students: 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 25. Which statement about these scores is correct?
questions.correctAnswer: The median is 8, and it describes the center better than the mean because the single score of 25 pulls the mean upward
distractors: The mean is 8, so the mean and the median are the same for these scores
The mode is 8, because 8 is the middle score in the list
The mean is lower than the median, because one very high score lowers the average
questions.explanation: Ordered, the scores are 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 25, so the middle score (the median) is 8 and the most frequent score (the mode) is 7. The mean is 72 divided by 7, about 10.3, which is higher than most of the scores because the outlier of 25 pulls it up. With a skewed set like this, the median is the better measure of the typical score.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One giant score DRAGS the mean up, but the median stays in the middle!

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of -0.85 indicates...
questions.correctAnswer: a strong negative relationship
questions.explanation: Values near -1 or +1 are strong; the sign shows the direction of the relationship.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Minus means they move opposite, and .85 is STRONG - like my roar!

questions.question: Which research method allows researchers to determine cause and effect?
questions.correctAnswer: The experimental method
questions.explanation: Only experiments manipulate an independent variable while controlling extraneous variables, allowing causal claims.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Experiment = cause and effect, because I CONTROL the variables!

questions.question: Random assignment is used to...
questions.correctAnswer: control for participant differences across groups
questions.explanation: Because assignment is by chance, traits like age, ability, and motivation are spread roughly equally across groups, so pre-existing differences cannot explain a later difference in results. Random assignment is different from random selection, which concerns who is chosen for the sample in the first place.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Random assignment shuffles people so groups start EQUAL!

questions.question: The placebo effect occurs when...
questions.correctAnswer: participants improve because they expect a treatment to work
distractors: a drug has no active ingredients
participants drop out of a study
questions.explanation: Expectation alone can produce real psychological and physical changes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sugar pill plus belief equals real improvement. Mind over matter!

questions.question: A double-blind procedure controls for...
questions.correctAnswer: both researcher and participant expectations
questions.explanation: Neither the researcher nor the participant knows who received the treatment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Double blind equals NOBODY knows. Two blindfolds beat one!

questions.question: Which of the following is an ethical requirement in human research?
questions.correctAnswer: Obtaining informed consent
questions.explanation: Participants must agree knowingly; deception is limited and debriefing is required.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Informed consent means they KNOW what they're signing up for!

questions.question: A researcher finds that ice cream sales and drowning deaths are positively correlated. The most likely explanation is...
questions.correctAnswer: a third variable (warm weather) influences both
questions.explanation: Correlation does not imply causation; a third variable often explains the link.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Correlation is NOT causation - look for the sneaky third variable!

questions.question: In a study of 200 students, the number of hours slept the night before a quiz and the quiz score had a correlation of +0.72. What is the best conclusion?
questions.correctAnswer: Students who slept more tended to score higher, but this study alone does not prove that the extra sleep caused the higher scores
distractors: The extra sleep caused the higher quiz scores for these students
The relationship is weak and negative, so more sleep went with lower scores
There is essentially no relationship between sleep and quiz scores in this study
questions.explanation: A correlation of +0.72 is a strong positive relationship: the two variables tend to rise together. Correlational research, however, cannot establish cause and effect, because a third variable (for example, overall study habits) could explain both, and the direction of influence is not proven by the coefficient alone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plus 0.72 means they rise TOGETHER, strongly - but correlation still is not causation!

questions.question: Operational definitions are important because they...
questions.correctAnswer: specify exactly how variables are measured
questions.explanation: Clear operational definitions allow other researchers to replicate a study.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Define it so clearly that ANYONE could measure it the same way!

questions.question: A researcher randomly assigns students to a new study method or to their usual method. The new-method group scores higher, and the statistical test gives p = 0.03. How should this result be interpreted?
questions.correctAnswer: The group difference is statistically significant, because a result this large would be unlikely from chance alone when p is at or below 0.05
distractors: The result is not significant, because significance requires a p-value above 0.30
The result proves the new method will have a large, important effect for every student
The p-value of 0.03 is the probability that the researcher's hypothesis is true
questions.explanation: In psychology, a result is called statistically significant when p is 0.05 or less, meaning such a difference would rarely occur by chance alone if there were no real effect. Here p = 0.03 meets that standard. Significance says nothing by itself about how large or practically important the effect is, and p is not the probability that a hypothesis is true.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: p of .03 beats the .05 line - the result is SIGNIFICANT, not just luck!

questions.question: A principal wants survey results that generalize to all 1,200 students at her school. Which sampling plan best meets that goal?
questions.correctAnswer: Randomly selecting students from the full enrollment list, so every student has an equal chance of being chosen
distractors: Surveying only the students eating in the cafeteria at lunch, because they are easy to reach
Surveying the first 50 volunteers who sign up outside the main office
Surveying only seniors, because they have the most experience at the school
questions.explanation: Generalizing to a whole population requires a representative sample, and random sampling gives every member of the population an equal chance of inclusion. The cafeteria, volunteer, and seniors-only plans are convenience or restricted samples, so their results may not represent all 1,200 students.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Random sampling gives EVERY student an equal chance - that is what lets results generalize!

questions.question: The part of the neuron that receives signals is the...
questions.correctAnswer: dendrite
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive incoming signals; axons carry signals away from the cell body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dendrites are receivers, like my ears catching your voice!

questions.question: The myelin sheath...
questions.correctAnswer: speeds up neural transmission
questions.explanation: Myelin insulates the axon, allowing the signal to travel faster.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Myelin equals insulation on a wire, makes signals ZOOM!

questions.question: An action potential is...
questions.correctAnswer: an all-or-none electrical signal traveling down the axon
distractors: a chemical released into the synapse
a graded signal that varies in strength
the resting state of a neuron
questions.explanation: An action potential fires fully or not at all; it does not vary in strength.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Action potential equals ALL or NOTHING, like my roar - full blast or silence!

questions.question: Serotonin is most closely associated with...
questions.correctAnswer: mood regulation
questions.explanation: Low serotonin levels are linked to depression and anxiety.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Serotonin equals the sunshine chemical for your MOOD!

questions.question: Dopamine is primarily involved in...
questions.correctAnswer: reward and movement
questions.explanation: Dopamine drives reward pathways; its loss causes Parkinson's symptoms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dopamine equals the REWARD chemical, your brain's high-five!

questions.question: A researcher wants to see which brain areas become more active, shown by changes in blood flow, while participants solve puzzles. Which technique should she use?
questions.correctAnswer: functional MRI (fMRI), which compares successive scans to reveal blood flow and activity in specific brain areas
distractors: Electroencephalography (EEG), which uses scalp electrodes to record waves of electrical activity
A case study of one patient with puzzle-solving difficulties
Naturalistic observation of people solving puzzles at home
questions.explanation: fMRI reveals brain function as well as structure by tracking blood flow, so it can show which areas are active during a task. EEG records the brain's overall electrical waves from the scalp; it shows timing of activity well but does not pinpoint active areas through blood flow the way fMRI does.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fMRI follows the BLOOD flow to find the busy brain areas!

questions.question: The frontal lobe is primarily responsible for...
questions.correctAnswer: planning and decision-making
questions.explanation: The frontal lobe handles executive functions like planning and judgment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Frontal lobe equals the BOSS, plans and decides!

questions.question: After a stroke, Mr. Lee speaks in long, fluent sentences that make little sense, and he cannot follow simple spoken instructions. Damage to which area best explains this pattern?
questions.correctAnswer: Wernicke's area, which is needed for understanding spoken and written language
distractors: Broca's area, which is needed for producing speech
The occipital lobe, which processes vision
The motor cortex, which controls voluntary movement
questions.explanation: Wernicke's area, in the temporal lobe, supports language comprehension. Damage there leaves speech fluent but meaningless and impairs understanding, which matches Mr. Lee. Broca's area damage instead makes speech slow and effortful while comprehension stays relatively intact.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wernicke's WRECKED understanding - fluent words, but no meaning lands!

questions.question: Damage to Broca's area would most likely cause difficulty with...
questions.correctAnswer: producing speech
questions.explanation: Broca's area controls speech production; Wernicke's area controls comprehension.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Broca's BROKE your speech - you can't TALK smoothly!

questions.question: The hippocampus is critical for...
questions.correctAnswer: forming new long-term memories
questions.explanation: Patient H.M. could not form new memories after hippocampus damage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hippocampus equals the memory PRINTER, saves new memories!

questions.question: The amygdala is most associated with...
questions.correctAnswer: fear and emotion
questions.explanation: The amygdala processes emotions, especially fear responses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Amygdala equals the ALARM, screams when there's danger!

questions.question: The sympathetic nervous system...
questions.correctAnswer: activates the fight-or-flight response
questions.explanation: The sympathetic branch arouses the body; the parasympathetic branch calms it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sympathetic equals STRESS mode, ready to FIGHT or FLIGHT!

questions.question: Endorphins are...
questions.correctAnswer: natural painkillers released during exercise or stress
questions.explanation: Endorphins reduce pain and produce the 'runner's high.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Endorphins equal your body's NATURAL painkillers, the runner's high!

questions.question: Split-brain patients (corpus callosum severed) demonstrate that...
questions.correctAnswer: the hemispheres can process information independently
distractors: language is in the right hemisphere
the brain cannot function when divided
memories are stored only on the left
questions.explanation: Sperry and Gazzaniga showed each hemisphere can work on its own.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Split brain equals two SEPARATE thinkers in one head!

questions.question: After an injury, a gymnast can still see, hear, and plan routines, but her movements are uncoordinated and she keeps losing her balance. Damage to which structure best explains these symptoms?
questions.correctAnswer: The cerebellum, which coordinates movement and balance
distractors: The thalamus, which relays sensory messages to the cortex
The hypothalamus, which regulates hunger, thirst, and body temperature
The medulla, which controls heartbeat and breathing
questions.explanation: The cerebellum, the 'little brain' at the rear of the brainstem, processes sensory input and coordinates movement output and balance, so damage produces exactly this uncoordinated pattern. The thalamus, hypothalamus, and medulla have the different functions named in the other options.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cerebellum keeps you COORDINATED - no cerebellum, no balance!

questions.question: The absolute threshold is...
questions.correctAnswer: the minimum stimulus needed for detection 50 percent of the time
distractors: the maximum pain a person can tolerate
questions.explanation: At exactly this faint level, a person detects the stimulus half the time and misses it half the time. The 50 percent point is used because weaker stimuli fall below reliable detection, so the threshold marks the boundary of what the sense can register.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Absolute threshold equals the QUIETEST whisper you can hear half the time!

questions.question: Weber's law states that the just noticeable difference is...
questions.correctAnswer: proportional to the original stimulus intensity
questions.explanation: The JND is a constant proportion of the original stimulus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Weber's law: the BIGGER the stimulus, the BIGGER the change needed to notice!

questions.question: Jae stubs his toe and finds that rubbing the skin around it makes the pain fade faster. Which theory best explains why rubbing helps?
questions.correctAnswer: Gate-control theory: activity in the larger touch fibers can close the spinal 'gate' and block pain signals from reaching the brain
distractors: Sensory adaptation: the pain receptors simply stopped firing because the stimulus stayed constant
Opponent-process theory: opposing pain processes cancel each other out in the spinal cord
Weber's law: the rubbing was a constant proportion of the original pain intensity
questions.explanation: Gate-control theory holds that the spinal cord contains a neurological gate for pain. Pain signals travel on small fibers that open the gate, while activity in larger fibers, such as the touch signals from rubbing, can close it and reduce the pain that reaches the brain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rubbing CLOSES the pain gate - touch signals shut the door on pain!

questions.question: The trichromatic theory of color vision proposes...
questions.correctAnswer: three types of cones for red, green, and blue
distractors: rods detect color in dim light
questions.explanation: The Young-Helmholtz theory says color vision starts with three cone types.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trichromatic equals THREE cones, like RGB on your screen!

questions.question: Gestalt psychologists emphasized that...
questions.correctAnswer: the whole is different from the sum of its parts
distractors: perception is built from tiny sensations
questions.explanation: Gestalt principles include proximity, similarity, and closure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gestalt: the WHOLE picture matters more than the pieces!

questions.question: As Sofia watches a door slowly swing open, the image the door casts on her retina keeps changing shape, yet she still perceives one rectangular door of constant shape. This is an example of...
questions.correctAnswer: perceptual constancy
questions.explanation: Perceptual constancy is perceiving objects as unchanging in shape, size, and brightness even as the retinal image changes with distance, angle, and lighting. Here shape constancy keeps the door rectangular despite its changing retinal image. The other options name unrelated processes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Constancy: the door STAYS a rectangle in your mind, even when its image skews!

questions.question: An example of a monocular depth cue is...
questions.correctAnswer: linear perspective
questions.explanation: Monocular cues like linear perspective work with just one eye.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Monocular: ONE eye is enough, like railroad tracks converging!

questions.question: The opponent-process theory best explains...
questions.correctAnswer: color afterimages
questions.explanation: Staring at red then looking away produces a green afterimage, supporting opponent pairs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Opponent process: colors FIGHT in pairs, stare then look away!

questions.question: The cocktail party effect demonstrates...
questions.correctAnswer: selective attention
questions.explanation: You can focus on one conversation in a noisy room and still hear your name.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cocktail party effect: your name POPS OUT of the noise!

questions.question: REM sleep is characterized by...
questions.correctAnswer: rapid eye movements and vivid dreaming
questions.explanation: REM is called paradoxical sleep because the brain is active while the body is still.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: REM equals Rapid Eye Movement, the DREAM stage!

questions.question: During a quiet class, 16-year-old Marcus suddenly slumps asleep for a few minutes, even though he slept nine hours the night before. These irresistible sleep attacks happen most days. Marcus most likely has...
questions.correctAnswer: narcolepsy
questions.explanation: Narcolepsy is marked by sudden, irresistible onsets of sleep during normal waking hours, which matches Marcus falling asleep in class despite adequate nighttime sleep. Insomnia is difficulty falling or staying asleep, apnea involves pauses in breathing during sleep, and somnambulism is sleepwalking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Narcolepsy: sleep ATTACKS strike in the middle of the day, no warning!

questions.question: After flying from New York to London, Priya is wide awake at 3 a.m. London time and exhausted at noon for the first two days. Her difficulty is best explained by disruption of her...
questions.correctAnswer: circadian rhythm, the roughly 24-hour biological clock that regulates the sleep-wake cycle
distractors: sleep spindles, the bursts of brain-wave activity seen in NREM-2 sleep
REM rebound, the increase in REM sleep after REM deprivation
general adaptation syndrome, the three-stage response to stress
questions.explanation: Jet lag occurs when the internal circadian rhythm, the biological clock running on a roughly 24-hour cycle, is out of sync with the new time zone. Priya's clock is still set to New York time, so her alertness and sleepiness fall at the wrong London hours until the rhythm resets.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Circadian means about a DAY - jet lag means your inner clock is in the wrong city!

questions.question: A sleep-lab EEG shows large, slow delta waves, and at that same time the sleeper gets up and walks around the room while still asleep. In which stage is this sleepwalking most likely occurring?
questions.correctAnswer: NREM-3, the deep slow-wave stage of sleep
distractors: REM sleep, the stage with rapid eye movements and vivid dreaming
NREM-1, the lightest stage between waking and sleep
NREM-2, the light stage marked by sleep spindles
questions.explanation: Somnambulism (sleepwalking) originates during deep sleep, which is NREM-3, the stage dominated by large, slow delta waves. In REM sleep the body is largely immobilized, so walking around does not fit REM, and NREM-1 and NREM-2 are lighter stages without this deep-sleep behavior pattern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sleepwalking lives in DEEP NREM-3, where the delta waves roll slow and big!

questions.question: Tolerance to a drug means...
questions.correctAnswer: needing larger doses for the same effect
questions.explanation: The body adapts to the drug, so more is needed for the same result.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tolerance: your body gets USED to it, needs MORE!

questions.question: In classical conditioning, the unconditioned stimulus...
questions.correctAnswer: naturally triggers a response without learning
questions.explanation: For example, food naturally causes salivation with no training needed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Unconditioned equals UN-learned, automatic like food making you drool!

questions.question: In Pavlov's experiment, the bell became the...
questions.correctAnswer: conditioned stimulus
questions.explanation: The neutral bell was paired with food until it triggered salivation alone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The bell LEARNED to mean food - that's conditioning!

questions.question: Positive reinforcement...
questions.correctAnswer: adds a pleasant stimulus to increase behavior
questions.explanation: For example, praise for good grades makes studying more likely.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Positive reinforcement: ADD something GOOD, behavior grows!

questions.question: Negative reinforcement...
questions.correctAnswer: removes an unpleasant stimulus to increase behavior
distractors: removes a reward to decrease behavior
adds a reward after a delay
questions.explanation: Taking aspirin removes a headache, so you take it again. This is NOT punishment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Negative reinforcement: TAKE AWAY the bad, behavior grows! (Not punishment!)

questions.question: Dana is paid once every two weeks, on payday, no matter how many reports she filed that week. She checks her bank app rarely at first and then constantly on the day before payday. Dana's pay is on which reinforcement schedule?
questions.correctAnswer: Fixed-interval, because reinforcement is available for the first response after a set amount of time has passed
distractors: Variable-ratio, because reinforcement comes after an unpredictable number of responses
Fixed-ratio, because reinforcement comes after a set number of responses
Continuous reinforcement, because every correct response is reinforced
questions.explanation: On a fixed-interval schedule, the first response after a fixed time period (here, two weeks until payday) is reinforced, which produces the classic pattern of little responding early in the interval and a burst of responding as the time nears. Ratio schedules are based on number of responses, not elapsed time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fixed-INTERVAL runs on the CLOCK - payday comes by time, not by count!

questions.question: A variable-ratio schedule produces...
questions.correctAnswer: high, steady response rates resistant to extinction
questions.explanation: Slot machines use variable-ratio schedules, keeping gamblers playing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Variable ratio equals slot machine, UNPREDICTABLE wins keep you pulling!

questions.question: At a packing plant, workers earn a bonus for every 10 boxes they seal, exactly 10 each time. This pay plan is an example of a...
questions.correctAnswer: fixed-ratio schedule
questions.explanation: A fixed-ratio schedule reinforces a response only after a specified number of responses, here exactly 10 sealed boxes for each bonus. Ratio means the schedule is counted in responses; fixed means the count never changes. Interval schedules would be based on time instead.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fixed-RATIO counts RESPONSES - every 10 boxes, every time!

questions.question: Observational learning occurs when...
questions.correctAnswer: behavior is acquired by watching others
distractors: animals learn through trial and error
questions.explanation: Bandura's Bobo doll experiment demonstrated learning by observation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Observational learning: MONKEY SEE, monkey do!

questions.question: After one meal at a new seafood restaurant, Tomas became ill that night from a stomach virus. A month later, the smell of that same seafood sauce makes him feel nauseated, and he cannot eat it. This one-trial learning is...
questions.correctAnswer: a conditioned taste aversion, a biologically prepared association learned after a single pairing of taste with illness
distractors: latent learning, because the learning stayed hidden until he was offered a reward
insight learning, because he suddenly understood the solution to a problem
learned helplessness, because repeated uncontrollable events taught him to give up
questions.explanation: Taste aversion (the Garcia effect) is learned after a single pairing of a taste with illness, even when the illness comes hours later. It reflects biological preparedness: organisms are primed to link taste with sickness. The other options describe different learning phenomena that do not involve a taste-illness association.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ONE bad bite can teach for life - taste plus illness equals lasting aversion!

questions.question: A teacher wants her student to write a full paragraph. She praises a single written word, then a full sentence, then two connected sentences, and finally a paragraph, rewarding only each closer step. This procedure is...
questions.correctAnswer: shaping, reinforcing successive approximations toward the target behavior
distractors: extinction, withholding reinforcement until the old behavior fades
latent learning, forming a cognitive map without reinforcement
negative punishment, removing something pleasant after each error
questions.explanation: Shaping is an operant conditioning procedure in which reinforcers guide behavior toward closer and closer approximations of the desired behavior. The teacher never waits for the full paragraph at first; she rewards each step that moves the student nearer to it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Shaping: reward each STEP closer, and the full behavior takes shape!

questions.question: Short-term memory has a capacity of about...
questions.correctAnswer: 7 (plus or minus 2) items
questions.explanation: Miller's magic number describes short-term memory limits.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Short-term memory: about SEVEN chunks, like a phone number!

questions.question: Chunking improves memory by...
questions.correctAnswer: grouping items into meaningful units
questions.explanation: Chunking expands the effective capacity of short-term memory.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Chunking: bundle it up, like packing a suitcase neatly!

questions.question: The serial position effect shows...
questions.correctAnswer: better recall for first and last items in a list
questions.explanation: The primacy and recency effects explain this pattern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Serial position: remember the START and END, forget the middle!

questions.question: Proactive interference occurs when...
questions.correctAnswer: old information disrupts recall of new information
questions.explanation: Previously learned material blocks newer learning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Proactive: the PAST bullies the present, old info blocks new!

questions.question: An algorithm is...
questions.correctAnswer: a step-by-step procedure guaranteeing a solution
questions.explanation: Algorithms are systematic and reliable but often slow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Algorithm: follow EVERY step, guaranteed answer (eventually)!

questions.question: A heuristic is...
questions.correctAnswer: a mental shortcut that is fast but can err
questions.explanation: Heuristics like availability speed up thinking but cause biases.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Heuristic: quick THINKING shortcut, fast but sometimes wrong!

questions.question: Functional fixedness is...
questions.correctAnswer: thinking of objects only in their usual functions
questions.explanation: It blocks creative problem solving with familiar objects.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Functional fixedness: stuck seeing a spoon ONLY as a spoon!

questions.question: The availability heuristic leads people to...
questions.correctAnswer: overestimate events that are memorable or recent
questions.explanation: Vivid news coverage makes rare events seem common.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Availability: if it's EASY to remember, you think it's COMMON!

questions.question: Divergent thinking is associated with...
questions.correctAnswer: creativity
questions.explanation: Divergent thinking generates many possible solutions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divergent: DIVERGE into many creative ideas!

questions.question: Language acquisition is easiest during...
questions.correctAnswer: a critical period in early childhood
questions.explanation: Children acquire language effortlessly during a sensitive period.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Critical period: little kids soak up language like SPONGES!

questions.question: Maslow's hierarchy places... at the base.
questions.correctAnswer: physiological needs
questions.explanation: Basic needs like food and water must be met before higher needs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Maslow's pyramid: FOOD and water FIRST, dreams later!

questions.question: According to drive-reduction theory, motivation arises from...
questions.correctAnswer: the need to restore homeostasis
questions.explanation: Hunger creates a drive that eating reduces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Drive reduction: fix the IMBALANCE, like eating when hungry!

questions.question: The James-Lange theory states that...
questions.correctAnswer: physiological arousal comes before the emotion
questions.explanation: 'I am trembling, therefore I am afraid' summarizes this theory.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: James-Lange: body FIRST, then feeling - 'I'm shaking so I must be scared!'

questions.question: The Schachter-Singer two-factor theory says emotion requires...
questions.correctAnswer: arousal plus a cognitive label
questions.explanation: The same arousal can be labeled as different emotions depending on context.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two-factor: racing heart plus LABEL equals emotion. Context decides!

questions.question: Intrinsic motivation comes from...
questions.correctAnswer: internal satisfaction in the activity itself
questions.explanation: Doing something for its own sake is intrinsically motivating.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Intrinsic: INSIDE joy, you do it because you LOVE it!

questions.question: The general adaptation syndrome (GAS) describes...
questions.correctAnswer: the body's three-stage response to stress
questions.explanation: Selye identified alarm, resistance, and exhaustion stages.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: GAS: Alarm! Resist! Exhausted! Your body's stress story!

questions.question: An approach-avoidance conflict involves...
questions.correctAnswer: one goal with both positive and negative aspects
questions.explanation: For example, wanting cake but fearing weight gain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Approach-avoidance: WANT it but FEAR it, like cake on a diet!

questions.question: Piaget's sensorimotor stage is characterized by...
questions.correctAnswer: object permanence development
questions.explanation: From birth to about age 2, infants learn objects exist when hidden.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sensorimotor: peek-a-boo! Learning things EXIST when hidden!

questions.question: According to Piaget, egocentrism is most prominent in the...
questions.correctAnswer: preoperational stage
questions.explanation: Children ages 2 to 7 struggle to take others' perspectives.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Preoperational: it's ALL about ME, egocentrism rules!

questions.question: Erikson's first psychosocial crisis is...
questions.correctAnswer: trust vs. mistrust
questions.explanation: In infancy, babies learn whether the world is safe and reliable.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trust vs mistrust: can baby TRUST the world? First crisis!

questions.question: Erikson's stage for adolescence is...
questions.correctAnswer: identity vs. role confusion
questions.explanation: Teenagers wrestle with the question 'Who am I?'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Identity vs role confusion: WHO AM I? The teen question!

questions.question: Kohlberg's preconventional morality is based on...
questions.correctAnswer: rewards and punishments
questions.explanation: At this level, right and wrong depend on consequences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Preconventional: what's in it for ME? Avoid punishment!

questions.question: Secure attachment is associated with...
questions.correctAnswer: responsive caregiving
questions.explanation: Ainsworth's strange situation research showed this link.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Secure attachment: reliable caregiver, baby feels SAFE to explore!

questions.question: The zone of proximal development (Vygotsky) refers to...
questions.correctAnswer: tasks a child can do with guidance but not alone
questions.explanation: Scaffolding from others helps children reach this zone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Zone of proximal development: ALMOST can do it, just needs a boost!

questions.question: Fluid intelligence...
questions.correctAnswer: involves reasoning and peaks in young adulthood, then declines
distractors: is the same as crystallized intelligence
questions.explanation: Crystallized intelligence (knowledge) keeps growing with age.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fluid: FLEXIBLE thinking, peaks young then slowly fades!

questions.question: Freud's id operates on the...
questions.correctAnswer: pleasure principle
questions.explanation: The id seeks immediate gratification of desires.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Id: the PLEASURE-seeking baby inside, wants it NOW!

questions.question: The superego represents...
questions.correctAnswer: internalized moral standards
questions.explanation: The superego develops as children internalize the rules and values of parents and society. It strives for perfection rather than pleasure, producing pride when behavior is good and guilt when it is not, and it often opposes the demands of the id.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Superego: your inner JUDGE, the moral voice!

questions.question: Projection as a defense mechanism involves...
questions.correctAnswer: attributing your own feelings to others
questions.explanation: For example, an angry person accuses others of being hostile.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Projection: PROJECT your feelings onto others, like a movie!

questions.question: The Big Five trait of conscientiousness describes someone who is...
questions.correctAnswer: organized and disciplined
questions.explanation: The OCEAN model includes openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Conscientiousness: CONSCIENTIOUS planner, organized and reliable!

questions.question: Humanistic psychologists like Rogers emphasized...
questions.correctAnswer: self-actualization and unconditional positive regard
questions.explanation: Rogers believed people have an innate drive to grow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Humanistic: HUMANS can grow! Unconditional acceptance helps!

questions.question: A projective test like the Rorschach...
questions.correctAnswer: presents ambiguous stimuli to reveal unconscious processes
questions.explanation: Inkblot responses are interpreted, but reliability is debated.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Projective: PROJECT your mind onto inkblots, ambiguous by design!

questions.question: Self-efficacy (Bandura) refers to...
questions.correctAnswer: belief in one's ability to succeed
questions.explanation: Strong self-efficacy predicts persistence after setbacks.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Self-efficacy: 'I CAN do this!' belief powers success!

questions.question: Generalized anxiety disorder is characterized by...
questions.correctAnswer: persistent, excessive worry
questions.explanation: The worry is free-floating and hard to control.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Generalized anxiety: worry about EVERYTHING, all the time!

questions.question: Major depressive disorder must include...
questions.correctAnswer: depressed mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks
questions.explanation: DSM criteria require a two-week minimum duration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Depression: TWO WEEKS of deep sadness or emptiness!

questions.question: Schizophrenia's positive symptoms include...
questions.correctAnswer: hallucinations and delusions
questions.explanation: Positive symptoms add abnormal experiences; negative symptoms remove normal ones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Positive symptoms: ADDED weirdness, like hearing voices!

questions.question: The diathesis-stress model proposes that disorders result from...
questions.correctAnswer: genetic vulnerability plus environmental stress
questions.explanation: Both a predisposition and a trigger are needed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Diathesis-stress: loaded GUN (genes) plus trigger (stress)!

questions.question: Systematic desensitization is used to treat...
questions.correctAnswer: phobias
questions.explanation: It pairs gradual exposure with relaxation techniques.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Systematic desensitization: baby STEPS facing your fear!

questions.question: Cognitive-behavioral therapy focuses on...
questions.correctAnswer: changing maladaptive thoughts and behaviors
questions.explanation: CBT is present-focused and evidence-based.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: CBT: fix your THOUGHTS, fix your life!

questions.question: Antidepressant medications primarily affect...
questions.correctAnswer: serotonin and norepinephrine levels
questions.explanation: SSRIs increase serotonin availability in the synapse.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Antidepressants: boost the MOOD chemicals!

questions.question: The Rosenhan study ('On Being Sane in Insane Places') demonstrated...
questions.correctAnswer: the unreliability of psychiatric diagnosis
questions.explanation: Healthy pseudopatients were admitted with schizophrenia diagnoses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rosenhan: fakers got LABELED crazy, diagnoses can be WRONG!

questions.question: Conformity is...
questions.correctAnswer: adjusting behavior to match a group
questions.explanation: Asch's line studies showed people conform to wrong answers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Conformity: go along with the GROUP, like Asch's lines!

questions.question: Milgram's obedience study showed...
questions.correctAnswer: most people obeyed authority even when harming others
questions.explanation: About 65 percent delivered the maximum shock.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Milgram: SHOCKING obedience, people followed orders!

questions.question: The fundamental attribution error is...
questions.correctAnswer: overemphasizing personality and underemphasizing situations
questions.explanation: We blame others' character but excuse our own behavior situationally.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fundamental attribution error: blame THEIR character, ignore the SITUATION!

questions.question: The bystander effect states that...
questions.correctAnswer: people are less likely to help when others are present
questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility explains this pattern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bystander effect: everyone WAITS, nobody helps!

questions.question: Cognitive dissonance is...
questions.correctAnswer: discomfort from holding conflicting beliefs
questions.explanation: Festinger showed people change attitudes to reduce dissonance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cognitive dissonance: mental CLASH, your brain hates contradiction!

questions.question: The foot-in-the-door technique...
questions.correctAnswer: starts with a small request, then a larger one
distractors: starts with a large then smaller request
questions.explanation: Agreeing to a small request increases commitment to a bigger one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Foot in the door: small YES leads to BIG yes!

questions.question: Prejudice is...
questions.correctAnswer: a negative attitude toward a group
questions.explanation: Prejudice is the attitude; discrimination is the behavior.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Prejudice: PRE-JUDGE with a bad attitude!

questions.question: Groupthink occurs when...
questions.correctAnswer: desire for harmony overrides critical thinking
questions.explanation: Janis studied groupthink in the Bay of Pigs decision.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Groupthink: harmony KILLS good thinking, nobody disagrees!

questions.question: The mere exposure effect shows...
questions.correctAnswer: repeated exposure increases liking
questions.explanation: Zajonc demonstrated this with repeated stimuli.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mere exposure: see it ENOUGH, you start to LIKE it!
